subject: Crunch Time
claim: Crunch Time taken from first seat and then copied by Reprise, Echo, Stunt Double and Greatest Hits lets one player place almost a whole round before anyone else moves.
evidence: Ava placed her first 4 minions in a row in round II (8 to 33 followers) and her first 5 in round III (39 to 83) before Ben or Cal placed anything.

subject: Most member colors
claim: One player reached the most colors possible in round I and took the contest every round with nobody contesting it.
evidence: Cal had 3 colors (the cap with 3 colors in play) after round I and won 4, 6 and 10 = 20 followers; Ava reached 2 only in round III, Ben never more than 1.

subject: Copyist
claim: Copyist pays +2 followers on every copy, including each step of a copy of a copy, so a copy chain pays it many times in one turn.
evidence: Copyist returned 18 followers on a cost of 5, 14 of them from 7 copies in 4 placements in round III.

subject: Hot Streak
claim: Hot Streak cashes a long run of turns in a row for a large one-turn payout.
evidence: Fired after four turns in a row in round III for +12 followers, 13 with its printed follower, for 7 resources.

subject: Cover
claim: Cover copying a rival's Overtime gave an extra minion and was the one moment anyone interfered with the copy engine.
evidence: Cal's Cover on Ava's Overtime gave +4 purple (a 5-pack), an extra placement worth about 6, and his third green minion tied green 3 to 3, a 10-point swing in a 5-point game.

subject: New Blood
claim: New Blood's +3 and the Yellow Cloak's +2 both trigger on the same new-color recruit, making a cheap member free.
evidence: Cal paid 5 for Early Traders and got 5 yellow straight back, then 4 more yellow from its two round starts.

subject: Buying followers
claim: With pack sizes of 1, 5 and 10, a recruit after a small space has only a 1-follower buy or a pass.
evidence: 6 of 21 follower buys were 1-packs and 4 recruits were passed to save up for the next pack.

subject: Went last
claim: Went last feels decided by who has minions left or who holds the token behind you, rather than by play.
evidence: The token changed hands 10 times; Cal won round II by counting that Ben had no way back, and Ben's minions were left at the end because his own Sleep In made them wait.

subject: Echo
claim: Echo copying the opener's Sleep In takes the token and almost the same haul, and the copied player gets nothing.
evidence: Cal's Echo got +4 purple, +1 green and the token; Ben spent On a Roll to retake it and still won Went last in round I.

subject: Overtime
claim: Overtime's extra minion looks strong but the token is taken at once and the extra minion lands somewhere ordinary.
evidence: Overtime paid Ava about 15 (a 10-pack plus the extra minion's 5-pack) against 9 for Crowd; its real cost was leaving Crowd, Build Up and Cover for Cal to tie green.

subject: Protesters
claim: Counting which spaces can take the token and shutting one with Protesters is a tense puzzle, though it shuts only one of several doors.
evidence: In round III it shut On a Roll and with Sleep In left Cal no way to the token: Went last +10 and Night Managers +2; in round II Ben shut the wrong door and lost +6.

subject: Consolation Prize
claim: Consolation Prize pays a player who is losing contests, keeping them in the game.
evidence: Paid 6 and 4 = 10 followers plus 1 printed for 7 resources.

subject: Last Callers
claim: Last Callers feels like a real answer to a token steal but went unused.
evidence: Never used; 1 follower for 7 resources, 4 fewer than a 5-pack.

subject: Closer
claim: Closer firing on the last placement and feeding a recruit feels like a plan clicking.
evidence: Paid 4 purple once in round II; in round III Ben placed last and it paid nothing.

subject: Harvest
claim: Harvest letting you pick colors one at a time fits an exact purchase.
evidence: Twice gave Cal exactly the colored cost he needed (Regulars in round I, Cosmopolitans in round II).

subject: Melting Pot
claim: Melting Pot pays something for a mix of member colors.
evidence: +2 followers and 2 resources for Ben, +3 and 3 for Cal.

subject: Makeover
claim: Makeover's rearrange had nothing riding on it when the next buy was followers, which take any color.
evidence: Both took Makeover only for +4 yellow before a follower buy and both skipped the rearrange.

subject: Buying followers
claim: No contest in this color set counts held resources, so piles are plain money and payment choices are forced.
evidence: Nearly every payment step was a single option; only Offering ever took resources (2 purple from Ben).

subject: Went last
claim: The Went last rim names a leader mid-round just because they placed most recently.
evidence: Ava was shown leading in round I with Ben's token minion still to come; Cal's standings showed him winning Went last that Ben then took back.

subject: Dabblers
claim: It is unclear whether Dabblers' wild members count toward Die-Hards' most green members.
evidence: The game counted them (Cal 4 green members to Ava 2) and Die-Hards paid +6, the difference between Cal 98 and a 92-93 loss, but both players guessed.

subject: Die-Hards
claim: Die-Hards returned more than a follower buy and decided the winner, though its owner believed it paid nothing.
evidence: 1 printed + 6 at game end for 7 resources; without the +6 Cal finishes 92 against Ava's 93.

subject: Offering
claim: Offering makes rivals discard by surprise.
evidence: Took 2 purple from Ben and nothing from Cal, who held only yellow.

subject: Recruiting members
claim: Picking a cloak first or second feels like a blind bet or automatic.
evidence: Three cloaks for three players; the last player took the one left.

subject: Recruiting members
claim: A focused one-color plan wins at most one contest a round while a spread-out cult wins several.
evidence: Ben placed 0 of 12 minions on green and had 1 member color all game; Ava's mostly one-color line still finished 5 behind the winner.

subject: Con Men
claim: Con Men has nothing to steal when nothing rewards holding resources.
evidence: Rivals held 0 to 2 resources each time Cal looked at it.

subject: Line Cutters
claim: Line Cutters gave first seat for a 4-cost recruit and protected the round III opener.
evidence: It mattered only in round III; in round II Ava had the fewest followers (8) and went first anyway.

subject: Copyist
claim: Copyist and Hot Streak are worth far more than their price to a copy player; generic guard members returned little.
evidence: Copyist 19 and Hot Streak 13 for 5 and 7 resources; Night Managers 4 for 6 and Last Callers 1 for 7.

subject: Recruiting members
claim: Members were under-used to contest Most member colors: one cheap member in a second and third color would have contested 20 followers.
evidence: A yellow member for Ava in round III would have tied the +10 (5 each), about a 7-point swing in a game decided by 5.

subject: Melting Pot
claim: The phrase 'colors among your members' counts grey members on Melting Pot but not on the Most member colors contest or Cosmopolitans.
evidence: Ben's Melting Pot counted 2 colors (purple plus grey guests) while the contest counted him at 1 the same round.

subject: Most member colors
claim: With 3 colors in play the contest caps at 3, which a player can reach in round I, after which rivals can only tie.
evidence: Cal reached 3 with three members costing 15 (5 refunded); Dabblers alone covers 2 colors.

subject: Turn order
claim: The Goes Last token produces long runs of turns for the players it skips, not only Crunch Time.
evidence: Round III order: Ava 5 in a row, Ben 1, Cal 3, Ben 1, Cal 1, Ava 1, Cal 2, Ben 3.

subject: Round end
claim: Round III decides the game.
evidence: 147 of 255 followers (58%) came in round III; Cal went from 41 to 98.

subject: Dabblers
claim: A wild member that fills a missing color makes later members of that color add nothing to the colors contest.
evidence: After Dabblers filled purple, Closer added nothing to Cal's member colors or Cosmopolitans (3 either way).

subject: Turn order
claim: Line Cutters and the fewest-followers-first rule point the same way early, so Line Cutters only overrides the catch-up late.
evidence: Ava (8) would have gone first in round II anyway; in round III Line Cutters took first seat from Ben (28).

subject: Survey
claim: Survey grows rich late when many minions sit on one color.
evidence: Cal's round III Survey paid 6 yellow off six minions on green.
